recorded_by: orchestrator (claude-opus-5), found on the gate's first live use, against its own repair
what: OW-10 requires that a repair be accepted as cured only on verification results BOUND TO THE EXACT RESULTING ARTIFACT plus a distinct-checker review. The gate as first written enforced the binding on the VERIFICATION side only. The distinct_checker entry carried attempt_id, execution_id, verdict and evidence_path - but no digest - so a checker that had reviewed an EARLIER draft satisfied the gate exactly as well as one that reviewed the shipped bytes.
why_it_matters: It reproduced, one level up, the very failure OW-10 was written to stop. The owner's words were 'verification results bound to the exact resulting artifact, plus the existing distinct-checker review'; a review of superseded bytes is not evidence about what shipped, for precisely the reason a stale test run is not. A gate that half-applies its own principle is more dangerous than no gate, because it certifies.
how_it_surfaced: Not by inspection - by using it. The first live cure claim was the orchestrator's own Ezekiel Phase-0 repair. The distinct checker (ezek_p0_recheck_a1#e1) reviewed the artifacts, RAISED further findings, and the orchestrator then edited the artifacts on those findings. So the review was stale by construction, and by the gate's own logic the claim should have been refused. Under the original gate it would have been ACCEPTED.
the_shape_of_the_error: The failing case was generated by the correct workflow, not by a mistake: a good checker raises findings, findings get fixed, and the fix invalidates the review that prompted it. Any repair round that actually improves something ends with a stale review. That makes this the NORMAL case, not an edge case, which is why it would have passed silently and often.
cure: distinct_checker.artifact_sha256_at_review is now REQUIRED and must equal the shipped artifact's live digest
two selftest vectors added and passing: 'checker reviewed STALE bytes' -> REFUSED, and 'checker review not bound to any bytes' -> REFUSED (selftest now 10 vectors, GREEN)
the gate's own docstring records that its author's first live claim was the failing case, so the reason survives a context clear
the refusal was NOT worked around: the orchestrator's cure claim stayed REFUSED and a second bounded review (ezek_p0_delta_a1#e1) was commissioned against the FINAL bytes
what_was_not_done: The gate was not loosened, no exception path was added, and the claim was not re-labelled to slip past. An owner directive's control is not something its implementer may grant itself relief from.
generalisation_for_later_books: A review is evidence about the bytes it read. Any record that certifies an artifact - a review, a sweep, a final check, a coverage statement - carries the digest of what it actually examined, or it certifies nothing. Look for the same gap wherever this campaign stores a verdict without a digest beside it.
impact_on_the_corpus: NONE. No row exists in Ezekiel yet and no cure was accepted under the incomplete gate. The gap was closed before the first acceptance, which is the only reason this is a control gap and not a defect.
dad_note: privacy-safe and generalisable: a verification artifact must be bound to the digest of what it verified, on EVERY side of the claim, and the omitted side is typically the human-shaped one (the reviewer) rather than the machine-shaped one (the test).
